title: Ask Spending with Apple Intelligence
description: Type a question about your Apple Card spending on iPhone, for example "Dining this month vs last". WalletFeed shows a chart, a list and a summary.

title: Background Sync
description: Send your Apple Card transactions to your destinations while WalletFeed is closed, with Background Sync and automations in Shortcuts on your iPhone.

title: Choose what a destination receives
description: Select which of your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions a WalletFeed destination receives, by account, category, merchant or amount.

title: Destinations
description: Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to an app, a spreadsheet or a file with WalletFeed. Add, test, change or remove a destination.

title: Export a CSV file
description: Export your Apple Card transactions to a CSV file on your iPhone with Export CSV in WalletFeed. You select a period, then save or send the file.

title: First steps with WalletFeed
description: Open WalletFeed on your iPhone for the first time and select the Wallet accounts that it can read. Then see your Apple Card transactions.

title: WalletFeed User Guide
description: How to use WalletFeed on iPhone: Wallet accounts, Spending, Ask Spending, Search, Recurring Charges, destinations, Background Sync and WalletFeed Pro.

title: Privacy and security
description: WalletFeed privacy and security on iPhone: the data that WalletFeed keeps, the data that it sends, and how to lock the app with Face ID.

title: Recurring Charges and alerts
description: WalletFeed finds the recurring charges on your Apple Card, such as subscriptions, and can send a notification when a new one starts or a price changes.

title: Search
description: Find your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions with Search in WalletFeed. Type a merchant, a category or an amount, or use Apple Intelligence.

title: Send previous transactions
description: Send your previous Apple Card transactions to a WalletFeed destination with Send History, and set the start date of new destinations with Initial History.

title: Siri and Shortcuts
description: Use Siri and the Shortcuts app with WalletFeed on your iPhone to open Spending, find transactions and send Apple Card transactions to destinations.

title: Spending widget
description: Put the WalletFeed Spending widget on your iPhone Home Screen or Lock Screen. It shows this month's total and last month's total to the same day and time.

title: Spending
description: Spending in WalletFeed shows the total of your Apple Card and Apple Cash purchases this month on your iPhone, by day, category and merchant.

title: Transactions
description: See your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions by month in WalletFeed on your iPhone, with pending transactions and refunds.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Correct problems with WalletFeed: missing cards, Ask Spending, Authentication failed, a sync that stops, and copies of transactions.

title: Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads
description: Share your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account with WalletFeed on your iPhone. Change the accounts and their start dates in the Settings app.

title: WalletFeed Pro
description: WalletFeed Pro lets WalletFeed send your Apple Card transactions to destinations. This page gives the prices and tells you how to change or cancel a plan.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to your app or server
description: There is no web API for your Apple Card transactions. iPhone apps read them with FinanceKit. WalletFeed sends them to a webhook, AWS, Supabase or BankSync.

title: Run a shortcut after each Apple Card purchase
description: Make a Shortcuts automation that sends each Apple Card purchase from your iPhone to your WalletFeed destinations in seconds.

title: See Apple Card spending by category
description: See your Apple Card spending by category on your iPhone, with the total for the month and the merchants. You can use it without WalletFeed Pro.

title: Add an Apple Card spending widget
description: Add an Apple Card spending widget to the Home Screen or Lock Screen of your iPhone. It compares this month with the same day and time last month.

title: Import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget
description: Import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget. WalletFeed saves them from your iPhone to an OFX file each month, and you import the file on a computer.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Airtable
description: Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to an Airtable base. WalletFeed adds each transaction as a record.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to AWS
description: Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Amazon S3, SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB or EventBridge in your AWS account with WalletFeed.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync
description: Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a BankSync table. Then your AI agents can read them through BankSync's MCP tools or REST API.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Coda
description: Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in Coda (Superhuman Docs) with WalletFeed and an API token.

title: Export Apple Card transactions to a CSV file automatically
description: Export your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file. WalletFeed writes the file in a folder that you select and updates it automatically.

title: Open Apple Card transactions in Excel
description: WalletFeed exports your Apple Card transactions to a CSV file on your iPhone. Excel opens the file on a Mac or a PC.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Firefly III
description: Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Firefly III with WalletFeed. Make a personal access token, then paste it and your server address.

title: Import Apple Card transactions into GnuCash
description: You can import your Apple Card transactions into GnuCash. WalletFeed writes an OFX file for each month from your iPhone, and you import the files.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Google Sheets
description: Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Google Sheets spreadsheet automatically with WalletFeed.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Linear
description: Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Linear with WalletFeed. Each month, or each transaction, becomes an issue in a Linear team.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Lunch Money
description: Send Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Lunch Money with WalletFeed. You paste a Lunch Money access token into WalletFeed.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Make
description: Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a scenario in Make, previously Integromat. A Custom webhook receives each month or each transaction.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Notion
description: Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Notion database with WalletFeed, for a budget in Notion.

title: Open Apple Card transactions in Numbers
description: Open your Apple Card transactions in a Numbers spreadsheet. WalletFeed saves them from your iPhone to a CSV file in iCloud Drive and updates the file.

title: Save Apple Card transactions as OFX files
description: WalletFeed saves your Apple Card transactions in one OFX file for each month. It updates the files automatically, and you import them into your app.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to PocketSmith
description: Get your Apple Card transactions into PocketSmith from your iPhone, with no file to import. Make a PocketSmith developer key, then paste it in WalletFeed.

title: Save Apple Card transactions as QIF files
description: Export your Apple Card transactions as QIF files. WalletFeed saves one QIF file for each month from your iPhone to a folder that you select.

title: Import Apple Card transactions into Quicken
description: You can import your Apple Card transactions into Quicken for Mac from OFX files that WalletFeed saves in iCloud Drive. Quicken for Windows uses a CSV file.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Supabase
description: Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a Postgres database in Supabase with WalletFeed. Each transaction is a row in your project.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Sure
description: Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Sure, the self-hosted budget app that is a fork of Maybe Finance. Make an API key in Sure, then paste it.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Toshl Finance
description: Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Toshl Finance. Make a personal token in Toshl, then paste it into WalletFeed.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to a webhook
description: Send Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a webhook in n8n or on your server with WalletFeed.

title: Get Apple Card transactions into YNAB
description: Import your Apple Card transactions into YNAB with the YNAB app for iPhone, or with an OFX or CSV file that WalletFeed saves on your iPhone.

title: Send Apple Card transactions to Zapier
description: Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Zapier with WalletFeed. A Catch Hook trigger starts your Zap each month or for each transaction.

title: Export Apple Card transactions
description: Export or download your Apple Card transactions from Wallet, card.apple.com or WalletFeed. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed can also update a file.

title: Find subscriptions on your Apple Card
description: See the subscriptions and other recurring charges on your Apple Card in WalletFeed. Get a notification when a new one starts or a price changes.

title: Guides
description: Step-by-step guides to send Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to budgeting apps, spreadsheets, files and automations with WalletFeed.

title: Search Apple Card transactions
description: Find a purchase in your Apple Card transactions on your iPhone with Search in WalletFeed. Type a merchant, amount or category, or use Apple Intelligence.
